Priya R: Quick thread — draft outbound for accounts affected by today's tokenization service lag. Need copy + link to status, mitigation steps, and confirmation on credit amounts. Draft below.

Priya R: ```Subject: Update on tokenization outages affecting some onboarding/ingest flows

Hi <CustomerContact>,

We wanted to let you know about a disruption earlier today that affected tokenization for a subset of onboarding and ingest operations. Our engineers identified a regression in the tokenization pipeline that caused intermittent 5xx failures and delays for new document indexing.

What happened: a deploy triggered an edge-case memory regression in the tokenization worker, causing elevated error rates for ~90 minutes (10:17–11:47 UTC).

Impact: customers performing large bulk ingests or first-time index creation may have seen errors or longer-than-usual processing times. Existing indices and inference for previously indexed content were not affected.

What we did: we rolled back the deploy, patched the tokenization worker, and performed a targeted requeue for affected ingest jobs. Our mitigation restored normal throughput by 11:47 UTC.

Next steps for you: if you see failed imports, please re-run the ingest job; we have queued replays for high-touch accounts and will surface results in the tenant activity feed. If you want us to re-run on your behalf, reply to this message and we’ll schedule it.

Compensation: we are offering a one-time credit equal to a single day of tokenization usage for tenants that experienced failed ingests. For enterprise customers we’ll follow up with tailored credits where appropriate.

Resources and help: status.redwood.ai (incident #2026-0323-TOKEN), office hours tomorrow 14:00 UTC for live troubleshooting, and a short runbook on retry best-practices attached.

We’re sorry for the disruption — we know time-to-activation matters and we’re taking steps to prevent regressions like this.

— Priya and CS Ops
```

Alex G: quick note — timeline in draft says 10:17–11:47 UTC. Engineering confirmed mitigation at 11:43 UTC (we should match). Also change "one-time credit equal to a single day" to "up to a single day" until legal signs off.

Sam T: add explicit link to the tenant activity replay page and a short checklist for customers who want us to re-run the job (consent, expected window, contact info).

Jordan L: +1 on re-run checklist. Also suggest adding a line for renewal teams: "If replays impact activation timelines for customers in renewal window, flag to CS leadership and we'll escalate to ENG-Priority."

Priya R: updated draft pasted below with Alex/Sam/Jordan edits — can Legal review final phrasing on credits?

Priya R: ```Updated snippet:
What we did: we rolled back the deploy and applied a targeted patch to the tokenization worker; normal throughput resumed by 11:43 UTC.

Compensation: we are offering up to a single day of tokenization usage credit to tenants with confirmed failed ingests. Enterprise customers will receive tailored compensation through their account teams. (Legal sign-off pending.)

Re-run request: to request a replay of failed ingests, please provide the ingest job ID, consent to re-run, and an available 2-hour window for our team to perform the operation. Replays will be completed within 24–48 hours.
```

LegalBot: Please remove any absolute commitment language like "will be completed within 24–48 hours" unless you add the qualifier "target window" or add an exception clause. Recommend: "Our target window for replays is 24–48 hours; we will update you if we need additional time." Also confirm incident number format is final.

Alex G: got it — changed to target language. Also Engineering asks to avoid promising requeue for extremely large ingests (>10M docs) without ENG ops approval. Could add: "For very large replays, we'll coordinate a custom plan."

Priya R: added both legal and eng notes. New draft below. Can I get final +1s so we can schedule outbound at 13:20 UTC?

Priya R: ```Final draft (to send):
Hi <CustomerContact>,

We wanted to let you know about a disruption earlier today that affected tokenization for a subset of onboarding and ingest operations. Our engineers identified a regression in the tokenization pipeline that caused intermittent 5xx failures and delays for new document indexing.

What happened: a deploy triggered an edge-case memory regression in the tokenization worker, causing elevated error rates for ~90 minutes (10:17–11:43 UTC).

Impact: customers performing large bulk ingests or first-time index creation may have seen errors or longer-than-usual processing times. Existing indices and inference for previously indexed content were not affected.

What we did: we rolled back the deploy and applied a targeted patch to the tokenization worker; normal throughput resumed by 11:43 UTC.

Next steps for you: if you see failed imports, please re-run the ingest job; we have queued replays for high-touch accounts and will surface results in the tenant activity feed. If you want us to re-run on your behalf, reply and include the ingest job ID, consent to re-run, and an available 2-hour window. Our target window for replays is 24–48 hours; for very large replays (>10M documents) we will coordinate a custom plan with you.

Compensation: we are offering up to a single day of tokenization usage credit to tenants with confirmed failed ingests. Enterprise customers will receive tailored compensation through their account teams. Legal sign-off confirmed on the phrasing.

Resources and help: status.redwood.ai (incident #2026-0323-TOKEN), office hours tomorrow 14:00 UTC for live troubleshooting, tenant replay page: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/<tenant-id>/replays, and a short runbook on retry best-practices attached.

If you believe this impacted any active renewals or critical activation paths, please tag your assigned renewal manager and we’ll prioritize follow-up.

We’re sorry for the disruption — we know time-to-activation matters and we’re taking steps to prevent regressions like this.

```
